Compare Sample-I.I.D. and Study-Disjoint Nested CV

Source: R/study_tools.R
stabl_multiomic_scheme_comparison.Rd

Runs stabl_multiomic_nested_cv() twice on the same data — once with sample-i.i.d. folds and once with study-disjoint folds — and summarises the gap between the two generalization estimates. A large gap signals that the sample-i.i.d. estimate is optimistic because held-out samples share study-level structure (e.g. outcome prevalence or feature shifts) with the training data.

Usage

stabl_multiomic_scheme_comparison(x_list, y, study_labels, ...)

Arguments

x_list

Named list of omic matrices or data frames with identical sample row names.

y

Named outcome vector (factor for classification, numeric for regression).

study_labels

Named vector assigning each sample to a study; names must cover exactly the sample IDs. Required.

...

Additional arguments passed to stabl_multiomic_nested_cv() (candidates, lambda_grid, metric, family, n_bootstraps, artificial_type, hard_threshold, stratified, random_state, n_lambda, l1_ratio, outer_v, inner_v, cv_workers, workers).

Value

A list with sample_iid and study_disjoint (the two stabl_multiomic_nested_cv objects), comparison (one row per scheme with balanced_error_rate, accuracy, and macro_f1), and ber_gap (study-disjoint minus sample-i.i.d. balanced error rate; positive values mean the sample-i.i.d. estimate was optimistic).

Details

Both arms receive identical arguments (including random_state), so the only difference is the CV sampling unit. Under stratified = TRUE the stratification is interpreted at the sample level for the sample-i.i.d. arm and at the study level for the study-disjoint arm, matching the semantics of each scheme.

See also

stabl_multiomic_nested_cv(), stabl_multiomic_study_diagnostics()

Examples

set.seed(6L)
ids <- paste0("s", 1:48)
y <- setNames(factor(rep(c("A", "B"), times = 24L)), ids)
x <- matrix(rnorm(48 * 4, sd = 0.5), 48, 4,
            dimnames = list(ids, paste0("g", 1:4)))
x[, 1:2] <- x[, 1:2] + 1.2 * (y == "A")
study_labels <- setNames(rep(paste0("study", 1:6), each = 8L), ids)
# study6 is outcome-skewed: sample-i.i.d. folds leak its composition
y[study_labels == "study6"] <-
  factor(rep(c("A", "A", "A", "A", "A", "A", "B", "B")), levels = levels(y))
cmp <- stabl_multiomic_scheme_comparison(
  x_list = list(rna = x), y = y, study_labels = study_labels,
  candidates = list(list(name = "rna", blocks = "rna")),
  lambda_grid = data.frame(lambda = c(0.2, 0.1)),
  outer_v = 2L, inner_v = 2L, n_bootstraps = 10L,
  artificial_type = NULL, hard_threshold = 1e-9,
  sample_fraction = 1, random_state = 6L
)
